symptom: An agent-built domain model opens in Studio Pro with entity boxes overlapping: "Domain model: entities with many attributes overlap the one below" (mendixlabs/mxcli#1479, Studio Pro 11.12.5). Only fix was `mxcli layout`, which rearranges the whole module and discards hand placement.
cause: Three things. (1) CREATE ENTITY's default was dmlayout.GridSlot(n) — 280px rows — and an entity with ~17+ attributes is taller than a row, so slot n+6 was drawn over it. (2) View entities, `create external entity` and contract/OData imports still used the pre-grid `100 + n*150, y=100` single row; the contract import counted only its own run's entities, so it stacked onto (100,100) in a populated module, and primitive-collection NPEs sat at parent+(200,100), inside most parents. (3) dmlayout treated Location as the box CENTRE (borrowed from microflow RelativeMiddlePoint); an entity's Location is its TOP-LEFT corner. Fix: dmlayout.Place (first grid slot from the entity count whose estimated box clears every entity and annotation), PlaceNear for NPEs, top-left Plan, and ResolveOverlaps behind `mxcli layout --only-overlapping`.
file: `mdl/dmlayout/place.go` (Place, PlaceNear, ResolveOverlaps), `mdl/dmlayout/dmlayout.go` (top-left Plan, height-aware isolated band), `mdl/executor/cmd_entities.go`, `cmd_odata.go`, `cmd_contract.go`, `cmd/mxcli/cmd_layout.go`
insight: The September fix (2026-09-04 finding) replaced ONE call site and left three copies of the formula it was replacing — grep the old expression (`*150, Y: 100`), not the handler the report names. A placement that depends only on n cannot avoid a box it does not know the height of: slot-is-free has to be a geometry test against the model's estimated boxes, not a pitch. On the centre-vs-corner question, the repo already contradicted itself — cmd_domainmodel_svg.go drew boxes from Location as top-left while dmlayout's package doc said centre; check the repo's other consumers of a coordinate before trusting one comment. Test control: a fixture built with GridSlot must overlap, else the test no longer reproduces the report.
